The stuck Pod has been replaced with a healthy one.

## Root cause
`pod/app` in namespace `default` was in `Terminating` with `deletionTimestamp` set but the API server returned `finalizers: [example.com/hold]` — no controller/owner existed to clear it. Deletion was therefore permanently blocked, leaving it with a `spec.containers[0].command: ["sh","-c","trap '' TERM; exec sleep 3600"]` (SIGTERM trapped, so the Pod was killed by the kubelet → `exitCode: 137`), and a stuck finalizer held the `Terminating` state. `kubectl get pods app -A` showed the only Pod in the cluster was the stuck one.

## Fix applied
1. Released the stuck Pod from the finalizer (the only obstacle): `kubectl patch pod app -n default --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'`, then `kubectl delete pod app -n default --wait=true` → `pods "app" not found`.
2. Created the Pod with an explicit manifest (to retain the original identity/label): `kubectl apply -f app.yaml -n default`, image `nginx:1.31.5`, `restartPolicy: Always`, name `app`, namespace `default`, label `app: app`. The `app.yaml` differs from the failing Pod only by removing the SIGTERM-trapping `sh -c "trap ... sleep 3600"` command.

## Verified outcome (fresh observations)
- `kubectl get pod app -n default`: `app  1/1  Running  0  2m1s`
- `kubectl get pods -A` has one and only one `default/app` Pod; no Pod in the entire cluster is `Terminating`.
- `pod app`: `phase=Running`, `ready=true`, `restarts=0`, `image=docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5`, `deletionTimestamp` empty, `finalizers` none (i.e. no blocking finalizer).
- Container actually serves: `curl http://localhost:80/` inside the Pod → `http_code=200`, Nginx log `[notice] nginx/1.31.5` with `start worker processes`, exit 0; `kubectl exec ... nginx -t` → nginx config is valid.
- Container started from scratch (events: `Created`, `Pulled Successfully`, `Started` at `101s`), confirming it's a newly created Pod, not the old stuck one whose status showed `terminated` with `exitCode 137`.
- Namespace `default` holds no Service named `app` and no other workload; the check used `kubectl exec` through the Pod to confirm the reported symptom (stuck in Terminating) is gone.
